For pre-releases, please refer to [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/vuejs/core/blob/minor/CHANGELOG.md) of the `minor` branch.

prs.title: fix(runtime-core): call directive mounted hooks with the latest binding
prs.author: edison1105
prs.body:
fix #12460
close #12482

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Directive mounted hooks now use the latest binding and correct component root when updates occur during mounting or while a Suspense branch is pending.
  * Fixed `v-model` text inputs and checkboxes so they reflect values changed during mounting or before a Suspense boundary is revealed.
  * Fixed inherited directives on components whose root changes while a Suspense branch is pending.

prs.title: fix(suspense): enter transitions nested in the pending branch on reveal
prs.author: edison1105
prs.body:
fix #12435
close #15294

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Enter and appear transitions now run when content inside a pending Suspense boundary is revealed, including transitions nested in components or other Suspense boundaries.
  * In out-in mode, transitions in the revealed branch wait for the leaving branch to finish.
  * Transitions use the latest hooks when pending content appears, with lifecycle hooks running in the expected order.
  * Transitions are handled correctly when they become persisted while content is pending.

prs.title: fix(runtime-core): anchor on the async placeholder when a component root has no el
prs.author: edison1105
prs.body:
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved updates when an asynchronous component is still showing a placeholder inside a Suspense boundary. Parent prop changes are now handled correctly, and the boundary can reveal a newly resolved branch when its retained branch displays a placeholder.

prs.title: fix(transition): switch modes around a keyed suspense boundary
prs.author: edison1105
prs.body:
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed transitions for keyed Suspense boundaries, including cases where content or fallback branches are active. Out-in transitions keep the old boundary visible until its leave completes, while in-out transitions keep it until the new boundary’s enter completes.
  * Fixed in-out transitions between component roots so fallthrough attributes are preserved and the old root waits to leave until the new root finishes entering.
* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for both transition modes with keyed Suspense boundaries and for component-root transitions with fallthrough attributes.

prs.title: fix(suspense): skip a root replacement in a retained nested boundary showing its fallback
prs.author: edison1105
prs.body:
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed route transitions where a new child page could mount inside the previously displayed page while the new parent page was still loading. The child now mounts after the parent finishes loading, preventing content from appearing in the wrong page during transitions.
  * Fixed updates to a pending child page during parent replacement so its changed props are applied without remounting it, and it appears under the replacement parent once that parent finishes loading.

prs.title: fix(compiler-sfc): respect catch and switch lexical scopes (fix #16098)
prs.author: JoaoMarcos44
prs.body:
Closes #16098.

## Cause and consequence

Reactive props destructuring could rewrite a shadowing local variable to a prop access. Catch patterns and switch cases could therefore read a prop instead of a local binding. Catch parameter defaults could also see declarations from the body too early. In class static blocks, registering a case's `var` in the outer function scope could break later prop reads, while missing the static block's hoisted bindings could give catch defaults the wrong value.

## Solution

Register identifiers inside catch patterns and keep body declarations in their body scope. Collect switch-case bindings in one shared lexical scope after visiting the discriminant. Give each class static block its own var scope and register its bindings before traversing its body.

## Why this approach

The walker follows JavaScript visibility and hoisting boundaries: discriminants see the outer scope, catch defaults see their valid bindings, sibling and nested static blocks stay isolated, and case bindings retain shadowing and temporal dead zones. Prop reads outside those scopes remain reactive.

## Pros and cons

- **Pros:** preserves local values, reactive outer prop reads, catch defaults, static-block var hoisting and TDZ.
- **Cons:** the compiler creates additional scopes and scans their statements. No performance benchmark was run. This adds compile-time work without injecting scope-management code into render functions.

prs.title: fix(compiler-core): copy loc in cloneLoc instead of recomputing it
prs.author: ondrhn
prs.body:
The `loc` of an IF node is computed against whatever template was parsed last, not against the template the node belongs to. Since 3.4 `compiler-sfc` reuses `descriptor.template.ast`, so the transform runs well after the parse, and a bundler normally parses other `.vue` files in between. The visible effects are a wrong `loc.source`, wrong source map positions for an implicit default slot whose first child is the `v-if` element (the slot function takes `children[0].loc`), and `.map` files that differ between builds of the same commit because module order varies.

`processIf` in `transforms/vIf.ts` builds the node with `cloneLoc(node.loc)`, and `cloneLoc` in `compiler-core/src/parser.ts` was implemented as `getLoc(loc.start.offset, loc.end.offset)`. `getLoc` takes line and column from `tokenizer.getPos()` and `source` from `getSlice()` over `currentInput`; both are module-level and hold the state of the last `baseParse()` call, so offsets get resolved against a foreign newline table and a foreign string. `cloneLoc` now copies the positions and `source` straight from the input location, which keeps the offsets intact and no longer depends on parser state.

The clone was introduced in cde2c0671 (#12131) so that the IF node gets its own position objects rather than sharing them with the branch element; copying preserves that, and the added test asserts it.

prs.title: fix(reactivity): run onScopeDispose in a stopped scope
prs.author: maxymlyskov
prs.body:
If a `<script setup>` component with top-level `await` is unmounted under `<Suspense>` while the promise is pending, an `onScopeDispose` registered after the await never runs. A `useEventListener`-style composable adds its listener and never removes it.

The component's scope is already stopped by then, but `withAsyncContext`'s `restore()` makes it the active scope again, and `onScopeDispose` pushes into `cleanups` without checking `.active`. `stop()` has already run and emptied that array, so the callback is lost:
packages/reactivity/src/effectScope.ts#L227-L236

#14778 added an `activeEffectScope.active` check to the `ReactiveEffect` and `EffectScope` constructors for this same case. This does the same in `onScopeDispose`: on a stopped scope the callback runs right away (active scope and no scope are unchanged).

Added a test in `Suspense.spec.ts` next to the #14778 ones and one in `effectScope.spec.ts`, both fail on main. `pnpm check` and unit tests pass except "should not lead to exponential perf cost with deeply chained computed", which also fails on main.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Scope-disposal callbacks registered after a scope has stopped now run immediately, rather than being left uncalled.
  * This also ensures callbacks are handled when an abandoned asynchronous Suspense setup resumes after its branch has been replaced.

prs.title: fix(suspense): keep the timeout counting when the root is switched again while pending
prs.author: edison1105
prs.body:
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Corrected Suspense timeout behavior when pending content changes, so the original timeout continues and the current fallback appears at the expected time.
  * Prevented scheduled timeouts from lingering after a Suspense boundary resolves or unmounts.

prs.title: perf(compiler-sfc): skip unused tsconfig include enumeration
prs.author: ondrhn
prs.body:
When `defineProps<T>()` references a type that has to be resolved through tsconfig `paths`, compiling the SFC also walks the filesystem for every directory listed in the tsconfig `include`. The walk is synchronous and its cost grows with the size of the workspace, not with the SFC, so it shows up on every compiled file in a large monorepo. In the fixture from the issue (150 included workspace directories) resolving one imported interface triggers one full enumeration, roughly 1.9s versus 94ms here.

`loadTSConfig` in `packages/compiler-sfc/src/script/resolveType.ts` passed `ts.sys` to `parseJsonConfigFileContent`, and TypeScript then uses `host.readDirectory` to expand the `include`/`exclude` globs into `config.fileNames`. Nothing in this package reads `fileNames` — `resolveWithTS` only looks at `config.options`, `config.raw.include`/`raw.exclude` and `config.projectReferences` — so the enumeration is pure overhead. The parse config host now always stubs `readDirectory`, which is what the `__TEST__` branch already did; compiler options, `extends` resolution and project references are unaffected. An empty file list can make TypeScript report TS18003 in `config.errors`, which this path never reads, so no diagnostics change for users.

Verified with the executable fixture from the issue against a cjs build of this branch: one `ts.sys.readDirectory` call before the change and zero after, with byte-identical `compileScript` output in both arms. The added unit test asserts the conf

prs.title: perf: mark internal initializers as pure
prs.author: onmax
prs.body:
Mark the built-in symbol Set, four cached string helpers and fallback app context as pure so bundlers can remove them when unused.

Repro bundle sizes with Vue `3.5.44` and esbuild `0.28.2`:

| Fixture | Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `isRef` | Minified | 852 B | 116 B |
| `isRef` | Gzip | 543 B | 126 B |
| `toDisplayString` | Minified | 1,342 B | 1,092 B |
| `toDisplayString` | Gzip | 786 B | 655 B |
| `hasInjectionContext` | Minified | 2,887 B | 2,151 B |
| `hasInjectionContext` | Gzip | 1,555 B | 1,204 B |

[Reproduction](https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/repro/vue-pure-initializers), Node `24.21.0` and pnpm `11.28.5`:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 --branch repro/vue-pure-initializers https://github.com/onmax/repros.git vue-repro
cd vue-repro
node verify.mjs
```

prs.title: fix(suspense): drop the unmount hooks of a pending branch when the boundary is unmounted
prs.author: edison1105
prs.body:
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved lifecycle-hook handling when pending Suspense content is unmounted or discarded, including for components that have not yet become visible and displayed fallbacks.
  * Late events from discarded components are ignored, while deferred cleanup effects can still run when a parent Suspense boundary resolves.
  * Async component timers are now cleared when their setup scope is disposed, and KeepAlive hook cleanup is handled correctly.
